titleEn: Poly-B Pipe Replacement in Vancouver: How to Know If Your Home Is at Risk
titleZh: 温哥华Poly-B管道更换：如何判断您的房屋是否存在风险
contentEn:
Homes built in Vancouver and across Metro Vancouver between approximately 1985 and 1997 may contain a plumbing material that is now well past its intended service life. Polybutylene (Poly-B) pipe was used in tens of thousands of Lower Mainland homes during those years, and it is failing — often without warning. Reno Stars has been replacing Poly-B piping systems in Vancouver-area homes since 2020, and this guide explains exactly how to identify whether your home is affected, what the replacement process involves, and what it costs in the current Vancouver market.

What Is Poly-B Pipe and Why Is It a Problem?

Polybutylene piping is a gray or blue plastic plumbing tube that was installed as the primary hot and cold water supply pipe in millions of North American homes between 1985 and 1997. In British Columbia it was widely used in detached houses, townhouses, and low-rise apartment buildings constructed during that window.

The pipe fails because the material degrades when exposed to oxidised drinking water — a process accelerated by chemicals such as chlorine that are standard in Metro Vancouver's municipal water supply. Over time the plastic becomes brittle and micro-cracks develop in the pipe wall. The fittings, which are typically copper or brass, also corrode. The result is both joint failures (causing leaks) and sudden pipe bursts, sometimes at pressures within normal operating range. Insurance companies in Canada began declining coverage for homes with Poly-B systems in the early 2000s, and many BC municipalities have documented the material in their infrastructure reports.

How to Tell If Your Vancouver Home Has Poly-B Pipe

The most reliable identification method is visual inspection of accessible piping. Poly-B pipe has several distinct characteristics:

  • Colour: Gray, black, or blue-gray plastic piping — not the white of modern PEX or the copper of older systems.
  • Markings: Most Poly-B pipe is printed with "Polybutylene," "PB2110," or "QEST" at regular intervals along its length.
  • Location: Look at the pipes entering your hot water tank, the main supply line where it enters the building, and any exposed pipes in the basement, crawlspace, or utility room.
  • Fittings: Poly-B connections typically use copper or brass fittings with a distinctive crimp ring visible where the pipe joins the fitting.

If your home was built between 1985 and 1997 in Vancouver, Richmond, Burnaby, Coquitlam, Surrey, Delta, or North Vancouver — or if you have a strata property built in those years — it is worth inspecting for Poly-B. A licensed plumber can confirm the material within minutes.

Poly-B Pipe Replacement Cost in Vancouver (2026)

Full re-piping of a Vancouver home involves replacing all accessible hot and cold water supply lines. The scope depends on whether the home is a single-family house, a townhouse, or a condo, and whether the pipes are accessible (open basement) or enclosed (concrete slab, furred-in walls).

Property TypeEstimated Cost Range (2026)Typical Scope
Single-family house (2 bath, 1,400–2,000 sq ft)$8,000–$18,000Full re-pipe, main floor + upstairs
Single-family house (3+ bath, 2,000–3,000 sq ft)$14,000–$28,000Full re-pipe, all levels including basement
Townhouse (strata)$5,000–$12,000Unit interior re-pipe; depends on strata bylaws
Condominium (unit only)$3,500–$8,000Visible supply lines only; limited access may increase cost

These figures reflect current material and labour costs in the Vancouver market as of 2026 and assume PEX (cross-linked polyethylene) as the replacement material — the standard replacement in Metro Vancouver. PEX is flexible, resistant to scale and chlorine, and carries a manufacturer warranty of 25 years or more.reno-stars-plumbing-replacement

Re-piping a Vancouver home is invasive work. It requires opening walls or ceilings to access the existing pipes, and the interior of the home is typically not habitable for the duration. Reno Stars manages the full process including municipal permit applications, wall repair, and final plumbing inspection by the City of Vancouver or relevant municipality.

The Replacement Process: Step by Step

Reno Stars follows a structured process for every Poly-B replacement project in Vancouver:

  1. Initial assessment: A licensed plumber inspects accessible pipes and confirms Poly-B presence. Reno Stars provides a written scope and cost estimate at no charge for Vancouver homeowners.
  2. Permit application: In Vancouver, re-piping requires a plumbing permit from the City of Vancouver (for work within city limits) or the relevant municipality. Reno Stars handles the application and coordinates inspection scheduling.
  3. Access opening: Drywall or ceiling panels are removed to expose the existing piping runs. Reno Stars photographs all work areas before any demolition.
  4. Pipe replacement: All Poly-B pipe is removed and replaced with PEX. Fittings are changed to new brass or poly-alloy connectors. The system is pressure-tested before walls are closed.
  5. Wall repair: All opened walls and ceilings are patched, sanded, and primed. Reno Stars coordinates with a finishing carpenter to return surfaces to their original condition.
  6. Final inspection: A City of Vancouver or municipal building inspector reviews the completed work and issues a plumbing final.

The full process typically takes 2–4 weeks for a single-family home, from initial assessment to final inspection.reno-stars-plumbing-process

Does Home Insurance Cover Poly-B Replacement in BC?

Standard home insurance policies in British Columbia have not covered Poly-B pipe replacement since the early 2000s. Most insurers treat Poly-B as a pre-existing condition, and homes with Poly-B piping are typically declined for new policies or are insured with a written exclusion for Poly-B-related water damage.

If you are buying a home in Vancouver, a Poly-B inspection is a strongly recommended condition of sale. A pre-purchase home inspection by a licensed plumber takes approximately one hour and costs $150–$400 depending on property size. If Poly-B is confirmed, this gives the buyer leverage to negotiate replacement before closing or adjust the purchase price accordingly.

Some BC stratas have begun funding Poly-B replacement as a common asset improvement, particularly in buildings where the association's insurance has become unaffordable due to Poly-B exposure. Owners in affected stratas should review their strata minutes and engage their property manager to understand whether collective replacement is underway or being considered.

Why Replace Poly-B Before It Fails

The cost of emergency plumbing response to a Poly-B pipe burst is not limited to the repair bill. A burst pipe in a Vancouver home can release thousands of litres of water in hours, causing structural damage to floors, walls, and finishes. mould remediation in a BC climate — where ambient humidity is already high — can add $15,000–$50,000 to a claim. Contents damage to furniture, electronics, and personal belongings adds further cost.

By contrast, a planned, scheduled Poly-B replacement at Reno Stars gives Vancouver homeowners control over timing, budget, and disruption. Work can be scheduled around family needs, and because the scope is defined in advance, there are no surprises.

Frequently Asked Questions: Poly-B Pipe Replacement in Vancouver

How do I know if my Vancouver home has Poly-B pipe?

Poly-B pipe is gray, black, or blue-gray plastic with printed markings such as "PB2110" or "Polybutylene" along its length. It was installed in homes built between 1985 and 1997. A licensed plumber can confirm the material within one visit.

Is Poly-B pipe dangerous?

Poly-B pipe is not inherently toxic, but it is at high risk of sudden failure due to material degradation from exposure to chlorinated Vancouver drinking water. A pipe burst can cause extensive water damage in a matter of hours.

How much does Poly-B pipe replacement cost in Vancouver?

A full re-pipe of a single-family home in Vancouver ranges from $8,000 to $28,000 depending on home size, number of bathrooms, and accessibility. Townhouse and condo replacement costs are lower, typically $3,500 to $12,000.

Does BC home insurance cover Poly-B replacement?

Most BC home insurers do not cover Poly-B replacement and may decline to insure a home with Poly-B piping. A pre-purchase plumbing inspection is strongly recommended before buying a Vancouver-area home built between 1985 and 1997.

How long does Poly-B replacement take in Vancouver?

A full re-pipe of a single-family home takes approximately 2–4 weeks from initial assessment to final municipal inspection, including permit application, pipe replacement, wall repair, and inspection.

What material replaces Poly-B pipe?

PEX (cross-linked polyethylene) is the standard replacement material in Vancouver. It is flexible, chlorine-resistant, and carries a manufacturer warranty of 25 years or more. It is approved for use in BC under the British Columbia Building Code.

建于1985年至1997年间的温哥华及大温地区房屋可能使用了某种已远超预期使用寿命的水管材料。聚丁烯（Poly-B）管道在这段时期内被广泛安装于数万套大温住宅之中，而它正在老化失效——往往毫无预兆。聚星装修（Reno Stars）自2020年起在大温地区承接Poly-B管道更换工程，本指南将详细说明如何判断您的房屋是否受影响、更换工程的具体流程，以及当前温哥华市场的实际费用。

什么是Poly-B管道，为什么它是个问题？

聚丁烯管道是一种灰色、黑色或蓝灰色的塑料水管，曾在1985年至1997年间被用于北美数百万住宅的冷热水主管道。在卑诗省，它广泛应用于该时期建设的独立屋、联排别墅及低层公寓楼。

管道失效的原因是材料在接触氧化饮用水时会降解——这一过程因大温哥华市政供水中的氯等化学物质而加速。久而久之，塑料变脆，管道壁出现微裂纹。连接件（通常为铜或黄铜）也会腐蚀。其结果是接头失效（导致漏水）和突发爆管，有时甚至在正常压力范围内发生。

如何判断您的温哥华房屋是否有Poly-B管道

最可靠的鉴定方法是目视检查可触及的管道。Poly-B管道有几个明显特征：

  • 颜色：灰色、黑色或蓝灰色塑料管道——不是现代PEX的白色，也不是老式系统的铜色。
  • 标识：大多数Poly-B管道每隔一定距离就会印有"Polybutylene"、"PB2110"或"QEST"字样。
  • 位置：查看进入热水箱的管道、入户主管道，以及地下室、爬行空间或设备房中任何外露的管道。
  • 接头：Poly-B连接处通常使用铜或黄铜接头，并带有可见的压接环。

如果您的房屋建于1985年至1997年间，位于温哥华、列治文、本拿比、高贵林、素里、Delta或北温——或者是该时期建造的共管物业——值得检查是否有Poly-B。水管工可在几分钟内确认材料类型。

温哥华Poly-B管道更换费用（2026年）

温哥华住宅的全面管道更换涉及更换所有可触及的冷热水主管道。工程范围取决于房屋类型（独立屋、联排别墅或公寓）以及管道是否可触及（开放地下室）或封闭（混凝土板、隐蔽墙内）。

物业类型2026年预估费用范围典型工程范围
独立屋（2卫，1,400–2,000平方尺）$8,000–$18,000全屋管道更换，一楼+二楼
独立屋（3+卫，2,000–3,000平方尺）$14,000–$28,000全屋管道更换，包括地下室
联排别墅（共管）$5,000–$12,000单位内部管道更换；视共管细则而定
共管公寓（仅单位内部）$3,500–$8,000仅可见供水管道；通道受限可能增加费用

以上数字为2026年温哥华市场当前材料及人工成本，以PEX（交联聚乙烯）为替换材料——这是大温哥华的标准替换方案。PEX柔韧、耐结垢、耐氯，厂家质保25年以上。

更换温哥华房屋管道是侵入性工程。需要打开墙壁或天花板以触及现有管道，工程期间室内通常不宜居住。

更换流程：分步说明

聚星装修对每个温哥华Poly-B更换项目均遵循以下结构化流程：

  1. 初步评估：持牌水管工检查可触及管道并确认Poly-B的存在。聚星装修为温哥华业主提供免费书面工程范围及报价。
  2. 许可证申请：在温哥华，管道更换需要向温哥华市政府（或相关市政当局）申请管道许可证。聚星装修代办申请并协调检查安排。
  3. 开口施工：拆除干墙或天花板面板以暴露现有管道走向。聚星装修在所有拆除前拍照记录工作区域。
  4. 管道更换：拆除所有Poly-B管道并更换为PEX。接头更换为新的黄铜或聚合金连接件。系统加压测试合格后再封闭墙壁。
  5. 墙壁修复：所有打开的墙壁和天花板均会修补、打磨并上底漆。聚星装修协调木工完成饰面修复，使表面恢复原状。
  6. 最终检查：温哥华市政府或市政建筑检查员审查完成的工程，并向温哥华市政府或相关市政当局提交管道最终验收。

整个流程从初步评估到最终验收通常需要2至4周。

BC省房屋保险是否涵盖Poly-B更换？

卑诗省的标准房屋保险自2000年代初起已不再涵盖Poly-B管道更换。大多数保险公司将Poly-B视为既有状况，可能会拒绝承保带有Poly-B管道的房屋，或以书面形式排除Poly-B相关水损。

如果您正在温哥华购房，Poly-B检查是强烈建议的购房条件之一。由持牌水管工进行的购房前检查约需一小时，费用为$150至$400，视物业面积而定。如确认Poly-B，买家可据此在成交前协商更换或调整购买价格。

部分BC省共管物业已开始将Poly-B更换作为共同资产改进项目进行资助，尤其是那些因Poly-B暴露而导致保险费用高企的物业。受影响共管物业的业主应审查其共管会议记录，并与物业经理沟通了解是否正在进行或考虑集体更换。

为什么应在Poly-B失效前进行更换

紧急水管抢修的费用不仅限于维修账单。温哥华房屋的Poly-B管道爆裂可在数小时内释放数千升水，造成地板、墙壁和饰面的结构性损坏。卑诗省高环境湿度的气候下，霉菌治理费用可额外增加$15,000至$50,000。家具、电子产品和个人物品的财产损失将进一步增加索赔金额。

相比之下，在聚星装修进行有计划、有安排的Poly-B更换，温哥华业主可掌控时间安排、预算和施工干扰程度。工程可围绕家庭需求安排，且因工程范围事先确定，不会有意外。

计划装修或需要更换老化管道？联系聚星装修获取免费、无约束力的报价。聚星装修已在温哥华、列治文、本拿比、高贵林和北温完成Poly-B更换及全屋管道更换工程。查看本拿比一个包含Poly-B全面更换的浴室装修完工项目。

常见问题：温哥华Poly-B管道更换

如何判断我的温哥华房屋是否有Poly-B管道？

Poly-B管道为灰色、黑色或蓝灰色塑料，沿管道长度方向印有"PB2110"或"Polybutylene"等标识。它安装于1985年至1997年间建造的房屋。持牌水管工一次上门即可确认材料类型。

Poly-B管道危险吗？

Poly-B管道本身无毒，但其因接触含氯的温哥华饮用水而导致的材料降解，使其面临极高的突发失效风险。管道爆裂可在数小时内造成广泛水损。

温哥华Poly-B管道更换费用是多少？

温哥华独立屋全面管道更换费用为$8,000至$28,000，视房屋面积、卫生间数量及可触及性而定。联排别墅及公寓更换费用较低，通常为$3,500至$12,000。

BC省房屋保险是否涵盖Poly-B更换？

大多数BC省房屋保险公司不承保Poly-B更换，并可能拒绝承保带有Poly-B管道的房屋。强烈建议在购买1985年至1997年间建成的温哥华地区房屋前进行购房前管道检查。

温哥华Poly-B更换需要多长时间？

独立屋全面管道更换从初步评估到最终市政验收约需2至4周，包括许可证申请、管道更换、墙壁修复和验收检查。

用什么材料替换Poly-B管道？

PEX（交联聚乙烯）是温哥华的标准替换材料。它柔韧、耐氯腐蚀，厂家质保25年以上，已获卑诗省建筑规范批准使用。
